title: Stock counts
description: Count a warehouse and correct its stock.

help.title: About Stock counts
help.overview: A stock count records what is actually on the shelf in one warehouse, then corrects on hand to match. It stays a draft until it is applied or cancelled. Applying it is the moment the numbers change.

sections.title: The draft
sections.body: Counting does not change stock. Applying does.
items: The count is for one warehouse.
Each line is a product, an optional variant, what was expected, and what was counted.
A blank counted quantity means that line was not counted. Apply leaves it alone.
Only a draft can be applied or cancelled.

sections.title: What apply does
sections.body: The difference is against on hand now, not against the snapshot from when the count was started.
items: Apply sets on hand to the counted quantity for every line that has a count.
Sales that shipped while you were counting are not undone, because the difference uses stock as it is at apply time.
Each change writes an adjustment movement.
A count below what is reserved for orders is accepted. Available can go negative. The shelf is what it is.

sections.title: After it is applied
sections.body: The count stays as the record of what was counted. The stock lives on the inventory row.
items: Cancel is only from draft. An applied count is not reversed from this page.
Look at Inventory for the new on hand, and at Stock movements for the adjustments.
Deleting a count is a soft delete and it can be restored.
